newsitem.title: USA: Western Atlas comfortable with EPS estimate.
newsitem.headline: Western Atlas comfortable with EPS estimate.

text.p: Western Atlas Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Alton Brann said Tuesday he is comfortable with analysts' consensus estimate that the company will earn $0.53 a share for the first quarter and $2.82 for the full year.
"I'm comfortable with that," Brann told Reuters following a presentation at the annual Howard Weil energy conference here.
Brann said the oilfield service company's core seismic surveying operation is on track for 20 percent year-to-year annualized growth through the first quarter.

The company is riding a wave of increased spending by exploration and production companies, particularly in world-class offshore fields and the deepwater Gulf of Mexico plays that have fueled recent record lease rounds, he said.
Capital spending budgets for exploration and production companies rose 12-14 percent this year. "We expect to fully participate in this robust market," Brann said.
The company expects demand for three-dimensional surveys in the Gulf of Mexico to continue, in part from the pending expiration of leases on inactive fields in the next three years.
"We have existing library data for many of those over 500 blocks," he said.
Analysts' estimates for first quarter earnings range from $0.50 to $0.56 a share, and for the year from $2.73 to $2.90, according to First Call.
Western Atlas posted $0.53 a share earnings in the 1996 first quarter, and $2.31 a share for all of last year, according to First Call.
